FICTIONAL TEST REPORT
RADIOGRAPH LEFT HIP AND PELVIS, AP
Date of examination: 08/05/2025
Clinical details: 81 year old, fall at home, unable to weight bear on the left leg.
FINDINGS:
There is a displaced subcapital fracture of the left femoral neck. The femoral head is displaced inferiorly and shows varus angulation, and the Shenton line is broken. The fracture line lies approximately 3 cm from the greater trochanter. There is generalised osteopenia. The right hip joint shows mild superior joint space narrowing. The sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis are intact, and no pelvic ring fracture is seen. The pubic rami are intact bilaterally. There is a small phlebolith in the left pelvis. Calcified atheroma is noted in the femoral arteries.
IMPRESSION:
1. Displaced intracapsular fracture of the left femoral neck.
2. Osteopenia and mild right hip osteoarthritis.
